target.name: ByteCodeInterpreter bit-array clearer (sub_08004396)
target.role: clear one bit of the byte array with a read-modify-write
target.notes: sub_08004396, 22 bytes and 11 instructions, one terminator at 0x080043AA, no calls and NO literal pool. It is the third and last member of the bit-array accessor trio, sitting immediately after the setter at 0x08004380, so the reader, the setter and this clearer tile 0x08004364..0x080043AC. DERIVED ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE, not by assuming it mirrors the setter: the differing instruction is `bics`, which computes byte & ~(1 << (value & 7)) - a bit CLEAR - where the setter uses `orrs`. The index split is the same as the other two: `asrs #3` selects the byte, the `lsls`/`lsrs #0x1d` pair isolates the low three bits, and the byte is at base + (value >> 3) + 0x55. The byte-index shift is ARITHMETIC, so a value with bit 31 set clears BEFORE the base. It is a READ-MODIFY-WRITE: `ldrb` reads, `bics` clears, `strb` writes back, so the other seven bits of that byte survive; exactly one byte is modified. There is NO BOUNDS CHECK and no NULL check. THE RETURN VALUE IS NOT DEFINED: the routine ends with `bx lr` with r0 still holding the computed field address, not a status or a boolean, so the reconstruction returns void rather than inventing a result. Clearing an already-clear bit is a no-op, and clearing the same bit twice equals clearing it once; both are asserted. UNKNOWN: what the bit means, and how large the array is. No semantic name is assigned and nothing is imported from another title.

boundary_evidence.method: aligned chain-walk from each entry, following local branches

functions.role: clear one bit of the byte array

trio.role: test a bit and return a boolean

gather.shift_amount_rule: ARM7TDMI register LSL: an amount of 0 leaves the value unchanged, 1..31 shifts normally, and an amount of 32 OR MORE YIELDS ZERO
gather.shift_bits_above_31_evidence: `lsls r0, r4` makes the shift amount the RUNTIME loop index, and the architectural rule for a register-controlled LSL zeroes the result at an amount of 32 or more, so every iteration at n >= 32 ORs in nothing and the mask can never carry a bit above 31 whatever the bound is
gather.shift_was_previously_wrong: an earlier revision of this report claimed the amount was taken modulo 32; that is not the ARM7TDMI rule and is corrected here
gather.has_bounds_check_evidence: neither the offset nor the bound is compared against any size; both are runtime values and no size is reachable from this routine

flag_state.gather_mask: bit n of the mask is the flag array bit at (offset + n), for n = 0 .. bound-1; a bound of zero or less yields a mask of 0
flag_state.gather_mask_destination: the mask is PUSHED back onto the VM value stack as the new top; it does not leave the VM in this routine
flag_state.gather_note: the value passed to the reader is `offset + n`, not `n`, so the offset is a BIT NUMBER in the array rather than a byte index or a pointer

array_extent.lower_bound_evidence: the trio's own index arithmetic addresses one byte at base + 0x55, and the boolean transforms only ever produce indices 0 and 1, so bits 0 and 1 of that byte are reachable and used
array_extent.upper_bound_reason: no instruction compares an index or an offset against a size, and the gather loop's offset and bound are runtime values, so no static upper bound can be derived from code evidence
